paras: Abronia cunemica, also known commonly as the Coapilla arboreal alligator lizard and el dragoncito de Coapilla in Mexican Spanish, is a species of lizard in the family Anguidae. The species, which was described in 2024 by Adam Clause et al., is native to southern Mexico.
Abronia cunemica is endemic to the Mexican state of Chiapas. The type locality is "vicinity of Coapilla, Municipio de Coapilla, Northern Highlands, Chiapas, Mexico".
Abronia cunemica is an elusive tree-dweller, feeding mainly on insects. It is rarely seen due to its limited distribution and ambiguous behaviour.
It can reach a length of up to 9.8 in (250 mm) and is characterized by its yellow-brown scaly body with darker brown blotches.
